interpretation.workflow: All four image builds, four SQL profiles, two helper pipe suites, four disk/capacity experiments and both kernel-OOM characterization profiles completed successfully at this source revision.
interpretation.source_recheck: The six P0 source/identity groups passed in all four profiles: tagged keys, bounded version/incarnation recheck, strict definitions/RLS refusal and quoted/bound inputs, active-statement and repeatable-read visibility, DDL/namespace guard plus pre-SPI cancellation cleanup, and internal ACL/runtime-superuser checks. These are fixture diagnostics; no production source authorization or synchronization is implemented.
interpretation.later_source_work_excluded: The later secondary-index inside-SPI cancellation group and explicit built-in heap table-AM restriction are absent from this tested commit. CI7 does not validate those changes.
interpretation.capacity: At exact 384 MiB, both already-flushed full-text config-save ENOSPC/recovery and independent clean reopen passed with all eight records/four representations, phrase and token-prefix queries. Allocated bytes rose from 34,963,456 before reopen to 220,508,160 after reopen; remaining capacity was 182,145,024 bytes. This is a tiny fixed fixture, not a product sizing formula.
interpretation.capacity_refusal: At exact 128 MiB, both full-text entry paths refused before engine open, filler creation or writes; before/after allocation stayed zero. This is successful guard behavior, not a successful 128 MiB reopen or recovery.
interpretation.historical_capacity_failures: CI5 and CI6 128 MiB full-text SIGBUS failures remain recorded. CI7 changes the supported experiment capacity to 384 MiB and characterizes 128 MiB refusal; it does not convert the historical failures into passes or identify a native fault instruction.
interpretation.oom: Two separate 768 MiB/no-swap containers produced exact memory-cgroup kernel victim records for the mapped target. Direct-worker death caused the expected PostgreSQL recovery/collateral loss; native-helper death preserved the supervisor and companion SQL under this experiment. Both retained the committed PostgreSQL marker and passed replacement 16-check Edge smoke. Retrieved inner reports have exactly one oom_kill, no group kill, target SIGKILL, zero supervisor/client/manual kill interventions and unchanged counters after replacement smoke.
interpretation.oom_evidence_limit: CI7's archive digest and every extracted member were independently verified. Inner observations, ready identity, native allocation records, outer result, PostgreSQL log and replacement engine report were cross-checked. The inner report correctly retains correlated_only attribution; the matching external kernel cgroup/victim messages support the outer strict conclusion. This controlled positive-oom_score_adj experiment does not establish production memory isolation.
interpretation.helper_fault_domain: Native-helper SIGKILL/abort containment is distinct from SIGKILL of the PostgreSQL supervisor, which caused PostgreSQL recovery and companion termination. The 125-second frozen-helper test is a recorded supervisor kill after a SIGSTOP fault, not native cancellation or OOM.
interpretation.count_scope: 19+21+19+25 SQL assertion groups and 7+8 pipe groups include repeated common cases. Nested 16-check engine smoke is one containing assertion group. The 23 normal engine tests, two child tests, 21 Python tests and three distinct OOM guard tests have separate scopes; none is a capability-completion count.

reproduction.runtime_provisioning: Use the exact fresh containers and capacity/resource limits in the committed workflow. Positive fault commands require their dedicated guarded environment; no positive fault was run while normalizing this evidence.

normalization.removed: Duplicate disk stderr/stdout tails and duplicate execution observations; incidental tmpfs mount device/inode numbers removed. Numeric storage observations, recovery results and capacity-refusal outcomes retained.
normalization.oom_attribution: Exact ephemeral container IDs, cgroup paths, host/container PIDs, start ticks, nonce and two kernel messages are retained because their relationships establish attribution; they are not credentials or user-controlled product paths.
normalization.inner_observations: One random owned PostgreSQL data-directory path per inner report is replaced with a placeholder. Duplicate armed data is omitted because identical content is retained in native_records[0]. All counters, identities, namespace/cgroup attribution data, memory samples, native progress and actual SQL/exit outcomes are retained. CI7 archive verification does not upgrade older archives.
